messages:
Conor: Heads-up — noticed a sharp latency bump on interactive sessions in ap-northeast during the 03:00-04:00 UTC off-peak window. Success rate for gpu-alloc went from 98% -> 83% around 03:12. Anyone else seeing this?
Marta: yup saw alerts. looks like a short surge of spot evictions + region maintenance? infra-bot posted a rolling reboot a few minutes earlier. :frowning: 
infra-bot: [notice] scheduled maintenance window started for ap-northeast-1: node-reboot group-3 (03:10 UTC). Estimated duration 8m.
Leo: that's probably it. But the timing overlaps with our autoscaler cooldown so replacements didn't spin fast enough. interactive queue waits hit the 120s TTL.
Anna: Do we have metrics on how many requests fell back to smaller models vs waiting?
Conor: quick query: ~420 interactive requests in window; 280 had >80ms extra queue time; ~60 auto-fell back to tiny-gpt via routing policy; 80 errors (allocation failure).
Marta: 80 errors is bad. For off-peak we rely on spot-heavy pools. Maybe eviction credits exhausted for the spot pool.
Bryan: Suggestion: temporary policy to prefer preemptible-balanced pools for interactive until maintenance finishes, then revert. Less cost, more stable during reboots.
Leo: We can also lower the interactive min_replicas during off-peak and rely on faster wakeups + burst capacity, but that increases cold-start latency. tradeoff.
Anna: Could we implement short-lived local fallback (client-side) to a tiny local LRU cache model or cached embeddings to handle <token_limit=16> queries? That would remove pressure immediately.
Conor: good idea. But product needs deterministic responses for some routes. For others, best-effort is fine. Need per-route fallback flags.
Marta: ops plan: 1) immediate: enable preemptible-balanced routing for interactive in ap-northeast, 2) reduce autoscaler cooldown from 5m -> 60s for that pool, 3) add temporary 10% reserved on-demand buffer for 30m. Anyone object?
Leo: fine with 1 & 2. 3 increases cost — prefer targeted 10 on-demand across zones not full percent.
Bryan: Agreed. Make it quota-based: reserve 10 instances (p4d-sim) across zone. cheaper than broad percent.
Anna: I'll open a quick runbook change and set a config flag: interactive.offpeak.apn_fallback=true; include list of routes excluded.
Conor: Also let's add a small exp backoff on the client side when allocation fails to reduce thundering. 200ms jittered retries x3.
Marta: Log snippet from scheduler at 03:12: ```ERROR: allocation_timeout cluster=ap-northeast pool=spot-gpu-3 wait_time=72000ms evictions=6```
Leo: That log shows continuous evictions during allocation. We need to also tune our spot bucket mixing: prefer stable-instance-types first, then cheaper ones. Current spread is too aggressive.
Bryan: For longer term: ops proposal to introduce a graceful-interruption signal to running containers so interactive sessions can checkpoint small KV cache into S3 within 200ms. Will reduce perceived failures.
Anna: design note: checkpoint API must be idempotent and low-latency. We'll prototype with Redis+S3 combo.
Conor: After immediate mitigations, monitor for 1h and then revert reserved instances. Set alert: if allocation_fail_rate > 5% for 10m -> page eng-oncall.
Marta: I'll push the temporary routing change now and update runbook. ping once done. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [action] route_config updated: interactive -> preemptible-balanced (ap-northeast) by Marta at 03:22 UTC.
Conor: thanks. folks, post-mortem: capture cost delta from reserved 10 instances and whether client fallback reduced errors. assign to Anna + Leo.
Anna: on it — will collect logs and surface numbers in #eng-infra after 1h.
Leo: Also adding a small autoscaler experiment (fast-cooldown) to our canary pool. If stable, roll to prod next week.
Bryan: tagging this for capacity-planning sync Friday. need new simulations for off-peak maintenance overlap.
Conor: perfect. closing the loop here — good rapid ops.
